successCriteria.description: `PgNotificationRepository` class exists and satisfies the `INotificationRepository` interface — all four methods (`findByRecipientId`, `findByRecipientIdAndStatus`, `create`, `updateStatus`) are implemented with correct signatures matching the interface.

`PgNotificationRepository.create` accepts `Omit<Notification, 'id' | 'createdAt'>`, executes an `INSERT INTO notifications (...) VALUES (...) RETURNING *` with parameterized placeholders, and returns the persisted `Notification` with generated `id` and `createdAt`.
`PgNotificationRepository.findByRecipientId` queries `notifications` table by `recipient_id` and returns all matching rows as `Notification[]` (empty array when none match).
`PgNotificationRepository.findByRecipientIdAndStatus` queries by both `recipient_id` and `status` and returns matching `Notification[]`.

`PgNotificationRepository.updateStatus` executes `UPDATE notifications SET status = $2, read_at = $3, ... WHERE id = $1 RETURNING *` and returns the updated `Notification`, or `null` when no row matches the id.

`NotificationService` class exists and satisfies the `INotificationService` interface — all six methods (`notifyLeaveSubmitted`, `notifyLeaveApproved`, `notifyLeaveRejected`, `notifyLeaveCancelled`, `getNotifications`, `markAsRead`) are implemented with correct signatures.

Each `notify*` method calls `repository.create` with a notification object where `type` is the correct `NotificationType` enum value, `relatedEntityType` is `'leave_request'`, `relatedEntityId` is `leaveRequest.id`, `recipientId` is `leaveRequest.employeeId`, and `status` is `NotificationStatus.pending`.
`NotificationService.getNotifications(recipientId)` delegates to `repository.findByRecipientId(recipientId)` and returns the result.

`NotificationService.markAsRead(id)` calls `repository.updateStatus(id, NotificationStatus.read, new Date())` and throws a generic `Error` (e.g. `new Error('Notification not found')`) if the repository returns `null`.

constraints: All database queries must use parameterized placeholders (`$1`, `$2`, …) — no string interpolation of values into SQL.
The repository must import `pool` from `../../shared/db/connection` — no other database connection mechanism.

The repository must define a `NotificationRow` interface with snake_case column names and a `mapRowToNotification` function converting to camelCase `Notification` — matching the pattern of `PgBalanceRepository` and `PgAuditLogRepository`.
The service constructor must accept `INotificationRepository` — no other dependencies.
The service must be stateless — it delegates all persistence to the repository and holds no mutable state.

The `LeaveRequest` type must be imported as a type-only import (`import type { LeaveRequest } from '../leave-request/leave-request.model'`) — matching the pattern already established in `notification.model.ts`.
outOfScope: Unit/integration tests for notification repository and service — these are produced in Phase 3c (LeaveRequest Controller, Routes & All Tests).
LeaveRequest repository, service, controller, and routes — these are produced in sibling sub-phases 3b and 3c.
Notification controller, routes, or any HTTP surface — the notification module has no controller/routes in the current architecture.

entityInvariants.invariant: Every Notification created through the repository has a generated `id` (string) and `createdAt` (Date) assigned by the database — the caller supplies only `recipientId`, `type`, `title`, `message`, `relatedEntityType`, `relatedEntityId`, `status`, and `readAt`.

A Notification's `status` transitions from `pending` (on creation by a notify* method) to `read` (via `markAsRead`). The `readAt` field is `null` until the notification is marked as read, at which point it is set to the current timestamp.

When created via a `notify*` service method, `relatedEntityType` is always `'leave_request'` and `relatedEntityId` is always the `leaveRequest.id` — notifications are always tied to a specific leave request.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Must return the fully-hydrated Notification (with id and createdAt). If the database insert fails, the error propagates to the caller — the repository does not catch or transform it.
